cards.text: Paul the apostle is wrapping up his letter to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He's planning a trip, and he tells them, "This is the third time I am coming to you." Friend, NOBODY has ever said "this is the third time" in a happy voice.

cards.question: Before he comes, Paul quotes a rule for settling things: "Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three ___."

cards.text: Paul already warned them on his second visit, and now, while he's away, he warns them again. That's not a reminder, friend. That's the reminder in ALL CAPS.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians that if he comes back, he'll go easy on everyone except the ones who sinned earlier. True or false?
Paul won't spare anyone, because the Corinthians are demanding proof about him. Proof of what?

answers.text: That Christ is speaking through Paul
That Paul learned from Peter in Jerusalem
That Paul was trained under Gamaliel

cards.text: Paul says Christ is not weak in dealing with them but is powerful among them. Then he points them to the cross.

cards.question: Paul says Christ was crucified in ___, yet He lives by God's ___.

cards.text: Paul says the same goes for him and the ones with him: weak in Him, yet by God's power they will live with Him concerning the Corinthians. Weak doesn't mean finished, friend, because I looked finished for YEARS in a junk drawer, and now LOOK at this mustache!

cards.question: The Corinthians wanted to test Paul. Now Paul tells them to examine and test themselves. What are they checking?

answers.text: Whether they are in the faith

cards.text: Paul reminds them that Jesus Christ is in them, unless they fail the test. And he hopes they'll realize that he and the ones with him have not failed it.

cards.question: Paul prays to God that the Corinthians won't do anything wrong. What is he hoping for in that prayer?

answers.text: That they will do what is right
That he will look like a good teacher
That their city will respect the church

cards.question: Paul says he can't do anything against the truth, only for it. He even rejoices when he is weak but the Corinthians are ___.

cards.text: Paul prays for their perfection, and that's why he writes all this while he's away, so he won't need to be severe when he shows up. It's the oven timer beeping BEFORE the cookies burn, friend.

cards.question: Paul says the Lord gave him authority. What did the Lord give it to him for?

answers.text: To gather the gift for Jerusalem

cards.text: Then Paul starts his goodbye: "Finally, brothers, rejoice!" All those warnings, and THEN he says rejoice, like a tough meeting at work where the boss walks in at the end with a box of cookies.

cards.question: In his goodbye, Paul tells the Corinthians to keep their distance from one another until he arrives. True or false?
At the end of his goodbye list, Paul tells the Corinthians the God of love and peace will be with them. True or false?

cards.text: Paul tells them to greet one another with a holy kiss. And all the saints send their greetings.

cards.question: Paul's last line is a blessing. It names the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God. What else does it name?

answers.text: The fellowship of the Holy Spirit

cards.question: After all his warnings, Paul's closing blessing is only for the Corinthians who have repented. True or false?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "this is the third time", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to finish the quoted line "Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three ___." That tests the wording of the line rather than meaning the baker can reason out. A question about what Paul is pointing to would test meaning instead, for example that a matter is settled by more than one witness, so his third visit settles things.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Paul's closing instructions in 13:11 are never told: aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. Card 15 tells only "rejoice," and card 16 is a false statement, so the baker learns only what Paul did not say. A story card or a choice card with the real instruction as its right answer is needed so the baker leaves knowing what Paul told them to do.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Verse 8 ("we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth") is told only inside the question of choice card 12. That card correctly cites only its right answer (13:9), so no card cites 13:8.
findings.question: When a verse is told only inside a choice card's question and isn't the right answer, does it need to be cited somewhere, for example by moving it to a story card? Or is it fine for it to go uncited?
